instructions: Dice the onion and the bell pepper into 1/4-inch pieces. Dice the ham if it isn't already. Slice the tomatoes.
Crack the eggs into a large bowl. Add the milk, 3/4 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Whisk with a fork until just combined. Don't overbeat.
Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the ham and cook for 2 minutes, until it's browned at the edges.
Add the onion, the bell pepper and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Cook for 3 minutes, until crisp-tender. Transfer the filling to a bowl and wipe out the pan.

Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in the pan over medium-high heat. Pour in half the eggs. As the edges set, pull them toward the center with a spatula and tilt the pan so the raw egg runs underneath. After about 1 minute it should be mostly set but still glossy on top.
Turn the heat to low. Spoon half the filling over one half of the omelet and scatter 3/4 cup of the cheese over it. Turn off the heat, cover, and leave it for 2 minutes, until the cheese has melted.
Fold the empty half over the filling and slide the omelet onto a plate. Cover it loosely with foil.
Wipe the pan, melt the last 1 tbsp butter over medium-high heat, and make the second omelet the same way with the rest of the eggs, filling and cheese.
Cut each omelet in half so there are 4 portions. Serve with the sliced tomatoes.
method_notes: No version has the 20 ratings the rule asks for, so this is a fallback. Spend With Pennies (5.0 from 17) is the lead: ham, onion and two peppers cooked first, then eggs, then cheese under a lid. Jessica Gavin (4.93 from 13) agrees on cooking the filling first so the omelet isn't watery. Written as two 5-egg omelets cut in half so a family of four eats it as dinner; the second omelet is why it runs the full 30 minutes. The ham is listed gluten free to keep the tag.
